```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 110,
  dev.args = list(bg = "transparent")
)
```

This page runs rallyr on its bundled **synthetic** sample, so every number
below is random by construction: patterns in these charts are not findings.
It shows what the package computes and how the charts read. The same charts
appear in the [browser app](../app/), where you can load your own sessions.

```{r load, message = FALSE}
library(rallyr)
```

## The data

- The sample is a *bundle*: one file of raw API-shaped payloads, six
  sessions (`?"rallyr-bundle"`).
- Players are called "Sample Player" and "Sample Opponent"; dates are in 2030.
- No real session is in the package.

```{r bundle}
path <- system.file("extdata", "synthetic_sample_bundle.json.gz", package = "rallyr")
bundle <- bundle_read(path)
bundle
bundle_players(bundle)
```

`bundle_to_tables()` parses each session with the same parsers and rules the
package applies to a live fetch, for the player you name.
`bundle_derived()` then builds the documented derived-data tables
(`?"rallyr-api"`). Nothing here needs a database.

```{r derive}
tables <- bundle_to_tables(bundle, me = "Sample Player")
derived <- bundle_derived(tables)
knitr::kable(
  head(derived$sessions[, c("session_date", "me_shots", "shots_in_pct", "fh_speed_mph", "bh_speed_mph")], 6),
  col.names = c("Session", "Strokes", "Accuracy (%)", "Forehand mph", "Backhand mph")
)
```

## Session trends

```{r trend, fig.alt = "Three small line charts over six sessions: stroke accuracy, stroke rate and stroke speed."}
plot_session_trend(derived)
```

- One point per session (same-day recordings are merged into one session).
- Each metric is a rate or a percentage, so a long session does not score
  higher just for being long.
- In the app a range slider limits this chart; it starts on the last three
  months.

## Rally length by drill

```{r rally, fig.alt = "Dots for each rally's number of shots in each drill, with a diamond at the median."}
plot_rally_length(derived)
```

- Rallies are the corrected ones: placeholder speeds removed, merged rallies
  split at long pauses, implausible rallies left out (`?dq_corrected_rallies`).
- The drill comes from `segment_session_shots()`, whose defaults describe one
  drill routine (a short-court warm-up, net volleys, cross-court rallies);
  recalibrate it for other routines.

## Stroke speed

```{r speed, fig.alt = "Box plots of your stroke speed in miles per hour for each drill."}
plot_stroke_speed(derived)
```

- Your strokes only, in each drill.
- Fixed placeholder speeds from the vendor are set to missing first
  (`dq_clean_shot_speed()`), so they do not pull a drill's median.

## Net clearance

```{r net, fig.alt = "Points for the median net clearance in metres per session and drill, one colour for you and one for the feeder."}
plot_net_clearance(derived)
```

- Median per session and drill, you against the feeder.
- The vendor does not say whether the height is above the ground or above the
  net tape, so compare you with the feeder, not with a rule.

## Pauses between strokes

```{r gaps, fig.alt = "Histogram of the seconds between consecutive strokes of a rally, with dashed lines at the two pause thresholds."}
plot_gap_distribution(derived)
```

- A rally is split where the pause is longer than the dashed line for its
  drill and the feeder hits next (`dq_params()`).
- A threshold must sit inside the pauses actually seen. One above every
  observed pause could never split anything, and the check would pass
  without checking.

## Use your own sessions

In R, save the raw payloads of a shared session, add them to a bundle and
write it:

```{r own, eval = FALSE}
files <- sv_download_raw("<your share link>", "raw")
bundle <- bundle_add_raw(bundle_new(), files[["match"]], files[["stats"]], files[["shots"]])
bundle_write(bundle, "my_sessions.json.gz")
```

Merging a newer fetch of the same session replaces the older copy
(`bundle_merge()`), and `bundle_to_tables()` accepts either player as "me".

In the browser app you can do the same without R:

- load your bundle (step 1);
- paste the share link and open the three links it shows, saving each as a
  JSON file (the vendor's server does not let a web page read them
  directly), then drop the files (step 2);
- enter your name (step 3), add the session, and download the updated
  bundle (step 4).

## Privacy

- Everything in the app runs in your browser; files you choose are not
  uploaded.
- The app makes no requests to other sites: no analytics, no proxy, no
  fonts or scripts from elsewhere. A build check scans the code we ship and a
  browser check lists every request the loaded app makes.
- The page carries a Content-Security-Policy `<meta>` tag, but that tag does
  not bind the Shinylive frame or the workers, so it is a second line, not
  the guarantee. The guarantee is the browser check: it loads the built site
  in a real browser that can reach no other site, uses the app (an upload and
  a merge), and fails on any request that leaves, workers and the service
  worker included.
- A bundle holds raw session data. Keep it private.

```{r info, echo = FALSE}
sessionInfo()
```
